entry_conditions: Drawer closed or on a demonstrated opening trajectory, target_pose observable, compatible drawer velocity and reachable arm configuration; normal entry has open fingers and high TCP near the drawer approach.
exit_conditions: Drawer near open_stop_m=0.300 m with near-zero velocity, fingers open after release, TCP clear and moving above/toward the tunnel, and the block unmoved.
overlap_role: Actions 300:440 are supervised for all twelve occurrences: 140 actions (7.0 s) covering post-handle retreat, free-space turn and initial tunnel descent shared with retrieve_tunnel_block.
successor_readiness: Switch to retrieve_tunnel_block when the drawer is open and stable, the handle is released and the arm has clearance. The retained tail permits a later switch when already over the tunnel.
failure_signatures: Drawer remains below the open stop, velocity remains large, fingers stay closed, TCP does not clear the drawer, block moves, or IK reports material residual/limit contact. No demonstrated trial establishes missed-handle recovery.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy through drawer-relative clearance if target_pose remains reliable; prefer the dual-anchor policy or successor once independent block-relative departure is needed. Preserve both causal frames across any switch.
limitations: These conditions guide the high-level agent and do not add success criteria. Finger width is not contact truth, and relative decoding does not guarantee reachability or collision clearance under large displacement.
